pthm-qft-free-observable-domain-limits.physical_scope: The selected flat four-dimensional real scalar bosonic and Dirac CAR Fock models, with their chosen vacua and bounded smeared observable algebras. Operator-domain and point-smearing conclusions are conditional on the named mathematical carriers. No interacting theory, pointwise field operator, coincident product, thermal trace, apparatus, or empirical outcome is asserted.

pthm-qft-free-observable-domain-limits:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, $\mu\ge0$, and the selected free-field model of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Use the four-dimensional affine Minkowski chart,
signature $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, length coordinate $x^0=ct$,
and inverse-length parameter $\mu$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. For an open
region $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, use the scalar and Dirac test functions and
bounded local observable algebras defined in
[[def-qft-free-field-observables]]: scalar tests are real members of
$C_c^\infty(O)$, Dirac tests are members of
$C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb C^4)$, and the Dirac observable algebra is generated by
even products of bounded smeared CAR fields and their adjoints.

For a real Schwartz scalar test $f$, the closure of $\Phi_\mu(f)$ is
self-adjoint on its exact Segal-field multiplier domain. The scalar number,
Hamiltonian and momentum operators and the Dirac Hamiltonian and momentum
operators have the exact maximal sector-sum domains stated in
[[lem-qft-free-domain-observables]]. In particular,
$$D(N_s)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
If $A$ is one of these self-adjoint operators and $\Psi$ is normalized with
$\Psi\in D(A)$, then its model mean $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and variance
$$\operatorname{Var}_\Psi(A)=\|(A-\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle)\Psi\|^2$$
are finite; this needs $\Psi\in D(A)$, not $\Psi\in D(A^2)$. The product
$AB\Psi$ is defined only when $\Psi\in D(B)$ and $B\Psi\in D(A)$.

If $O_1,O_2$ are open regions and
$\eta_{ab}(x-y)^a(x-y)^b>0$ for every $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, then the
scalar Weyl algebras of the two regions commute, and the even local Dirac
algebras of the two regions commute. These are algebraic properties of the
specified free representations.

The chosen construction supplies only test-smeared fields and does not define
$\Phi_\mu(x)$, $\Psi(x)$, or coincident diagonal products. Fix a point
$x_0\in\mathbb R^4$ and a nonnegative normalized Schwartz Gaussian
$\rho\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$, and put
$\rho_{\epsilon,x_0}(x)=\epsilon^{-4}\rho((x-x_0)/\epsilon)$. These tests
approximate $\delta_{x_0}$ on Schwartz functions, but
$\|\Phi_\mu(\rho_{\epsilon,x_0})\Omega\|\to\infty$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.
For an equal-time Dirac field, fix a unit spinor $z$ and a nonnegative
normalized Schwartz Gaussian $\sigma$ on $\mathbb R^3$, and put
$u_{\epsilon,x_0}(\mathbf x)=\epsilon^{-3}
\sigma((\mathbf x-\mathbf x_0)/\epsilon)z$. These tests approximate a
spatial point mass, while $\|\Psi_t(u_{\epsilon,x_0})\|\to\infty$. Neither
family has a finite limit in its respective Fock or operator-norm topology.
This restriction does not rule out other distributional or renormalized
constructions. The Born interpretation of
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]] applies only after a density
state and normalized finite bounded instrument have actually been supplied;
this item reports no apparatus or outcome.

pthm-qft-classical-quantum-free-correspo.physical_scope: The selected flat four-dimensional free real scalar and Dirac models, with the stated (-+++) signature, inverse-length mass parameter and chosen Fock representations. The result matches compact-variation classical equations with weak test equations of the adopted representations. It does not derive quantization, a general spin-statistics rule, interacting dynamics, empirical validity, or a measurement outcome.

pthm-qft-classical-quantum-free-correspo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the selected free-field model of
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], using the metric, length coordinates, inverse-
length parameter $\mu\ge0$, field dimensions and Clifford convention fixed by
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. The classical scalar field
$\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and real; the classical
Dirac field $\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ is smooth with
commuting components. Their adopted free actions are the scalar and Dirac
functionals stated in [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Action symbols are used
only through compactly supported smooth variations, so no global
integrability of the classical background fields is assumed.

The compact-variation stationarity equations are
$$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0,\qquad (i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0,$$
with $\Box=-\partial_0^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. In the separately adopted
scalar and Dirac Fock representations, the corresponding weak test equations
are, for $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ and
$F\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$,
$$\Phi_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0,\qquad \Psi\!\left((i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F\right)=0.$$
Here “weak test equation” means precisely that smearing the constructed field
with the displayed differential operator gives the zero operator on its
stated common domain. With $h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$,
$\gamma^0=\beta$, and $\gamma^j=\beta\alpha^j$ as adopted in
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], the Dirac test operator is equivalent to
$i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu$.

Thus the classical action equations and the tested equations of the selected
free representations have the same differential expressions at these
normalizations. The Fock representation, species/statistics assignments and
vacua are additional physical model assumptions; they are not deductions from
the classical actions. No empirical outcome or measurement is asserted.

cex-qft-point-operator-assumption.physical_scope: The normalized Gaussian spacetime-smearing family for the real scalar field in the selected four-dimensional free Fock vacuum. It refutes only convergence in this representation's vacuum-vector norm; distributional or renormalized point-field constructions in other senses are outside scope. No empirical observation is asserted.
